Updated assessment leveraging Beige Book insights:

- Policy stance: The FOMC raised the target range to 4.25–4.50% and signaled “ongoing increases,” with continued balance sheet runoff—reinforcing a restrictive, inflation-fighting posture.
- Credit channel (SLOOS): Broad-based tightening in lending standards and weaker loan demand across C&I and CRE; tighter consumer credit and higher approval thresholds point to credit rationing. Banks cite a weaker macro outlook and elevated recession risk.
- Beige Book corroboration:
  - Activity: Multiple districts report flat-to-slower growth with mounting expectations of a 2023 downturn.
  - Sector mix: Real estate notably weakened (e.g., Boston/New York highlights), while some consumer-facing categories (restaurants) show resilience but are not broad-based enough to offset softness elsewhere.
  - Banking/finance: Regional banks note weaker loan demand, tighter credit, and rising delinquencies, reinforcing the SLOOS signal of a tightening bank-lending channel.
  - Labor/prices: Labor conditions remain tight but are easing at the margin; price pressures remain elevated though some moderation is noted in pace.

Implication: The Beige Book amplifies the downside growth risks already flagged by SLOOS and aligns with a restrictive policy backdrop. While there are pockets of demand, the breadth of credit tightening, real estate weakness, and cautious business sentiment shift the balance more negative than an FOMC-statement-only read.

Adjusted view: Moderately-to-meaningfully negative, tilted further down on Beige Book evidence.
